title: Plasma closes windows one by one on Wayland during restart -> losing browser tabs
line: Browsers that opt in through their desktop file now keep all their windows when you log out or restart.
explanation: On Wayland logout, plasma-shutdown asks KWin (org.kde.KWin.Session.closeWaylandWindows) to close every remaining window, and KWin sends xdg_toplevel.close to each one. Browsers handle each of those as the user closing that window while others are still open, so they drop it from their saved session and only the last window comes back (Chrome, Flatpak Chromium and Firefox all lose windows on master). Now an app can opt in with X-KDE-Wayland-TerminateOnLogout=true in its desktop file: KWin then sends SIGTERM once to its process instead of closing its windows one by one, and Chromium-based browsers handle that as a whole-app quit that keeps every window, as at the end of an X11 session. Apps that don't opt in still get the normal close request, with their own prompts and KWin's 'did not close' notification.

commits.message:
sm: Let apps opt in to SIGTERM instead of window closes at logout

Closing a browser's windows one by one made it forget all but the last
one on the next start. Apps that set X-KDE-Wayland-TerminateOnLogout in
their desktop file now get SIGTERM instead and can quit as a whole.

BUG: 511236

media.caption: Master, Chrome: windows A (2 tabs), B and C open (left); after the logout close and starting Chrome again only C comes back (right)
With the fix and the key in Chrome's desktop file, same steps: A (with both tabs), B and C all come back
Master, Flatpak Chromium (org.chromium.Chromium): A, B and C open; only C comes back
With the fix and the key, Flatpak Chromium: all three windows come back
Master, Chrome with unsaved text in a page that asks before leaving: logout shows 'Leave site?' and KWin's 'did not close' notification
With the fix and the key, same page: Chrome quits at once without the prompt and the page comes back without the typed text, as at the end of an X11 session
